transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-09
Time: 14:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Ruiz (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CTO, Mera), Priya Shah (Head of ML), Diego Morales (Infra Lead)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros?
[00:08] Liam: Hi, Liam here, CTO at Mera, we run a conversational commerce assistant across web and mobile, trying to figure out inference options.
[00:14] Priya: Priya, Head of ML, we own models and evaluation. We're concerned about p95 latency for streaming responses and overall tokens per second.
[00:20] Elena: Elena Ruiz, I'm the SE on the account, I'll dig into performance and benchmark details with you.
[00:27] Diego: Diego, infra. I'll be vetting VPC, egress, and network constraints.

[00:35] Samir: Great. Today's goal: understand your latency/throughput targets, concurrency patterns, and whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private makes sense. We'll also cover streaming behavior and what success looks like.

[00:50] Priya: To set context — production traffic is about 250 qps at peak across all our endpoints, but a lot is short chat sessions. For the personalization assistant, we want p95 generation latency under 300ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens) when streaming, ideally lower if possible.
[01:12] Elena: Just to clarify, 300ms p95 for streaming end-to-first-byte or end-to-end generation?
[01:18] Priya: End-to-first-token ideally, yes. Streaming matters because our UI displays tokens as they arrive.
[01:25] Elena: Understood. For Redwood hosted we typically quote p95 first-byte numbers in the 150–400ms range depending on model and model size; dedicated gets more predictable SLOs since you control the pool.

[01:40] Liam: The real question is cost. We want predictability — spikes during promotions double traffic for 20–30 minutes. Can Redwood handle bursts without sacrificing p95?
[01:52] Samir: Yes — we have auto-burst options on Dedicated, and Hosted uses smart routing and fallback to smaller variants. We can also do prefix caching for repeated prompts to reduce cost and latency.

[02:05] Diego: On Private, our security team might prefer that but we'll need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs. Also curious about network egress — if private on-prem we may avoid egress but hosted will have egress costs.
[02:18] Elena: We support KMS integrations and provide audit logs; I'll share the security pack. For egress we can measure expected charges; Dedicated in customer VPC reduces that but deployment details matter.

[02:32] Priya: For benchmarking, we need tokens/sec numbers. Our short prompts average 40 tokens; long ones up to 512 in a small percent. Can you show expected tokens/sec per GPU / per instance?
[02:45] Elena: It depends on the model and quantization. For example, a popular Llama-like 7B run on our optimized runtime with int8 quantization can do around 350–550 tokens/sec single-stream on an A100-ish equivalent in dedicated config; with batching you can hit 10k+ tokens/sec across a pool. But single-request p95 has to be preserved for streaming.
[03:10] Liam: Those numbers help. For our user experience we need p95 under 300ms for short tokens, but for longer responses p95 under 1.5s is acceptable. We prefer Hosted first to iterate, then move to Dedicated for cost predictability.

[03:25] Samir: That's a common path. For Hosted we can run a pilot using your prompt set to capture real p95 and token/sec. It'll give concrete numbers for planning.

[03:34] Priya: How do you instrument p95? Do you provide token-level latency breakdowns in Console?
[03:39] Elena: Yes, we report end-to-first-byte, per-token throughput, jitter, and KV cache hit rates. Console shows token-level cost and latency — we can also give traces for specific requests.

[03:52] Diego: For concurrency — our front-end opens 8 concurrent streams per user during heavy pages. Multiply that by clients, we can hit 400–600 concurrent connections. Does Redwood put limits per route?
[04:04] Samir: We enforce per-account and per-route quotas, but Dedicated can raise those limits. We also support connection pooling and long-lived streams to reduce connection churn.

[04:16] Priya: On fallback behavior — if a Dedicated pool is saturated, do requests route to Hosted? What's the impact on latency SLA?
[04:23] Elena: We can configure automatic fallback to hosted or to a smaller-variant model. Fallback will typically increase latency, so policies can be set: fail-fast, degrade gracefully (shorter output), or queue briefly. We recommend canary traffic policies during rollouts.

[04:37] Liam: About streaming: how does Redwood handle partial token buffering — do you emit tokens as soon as generated or after chunking? We worry about perceived latency if there's a 200–300ms chunking delay.
[04:48] Elena: We stream as tokens are produced; small chunk sizes help perceived latency. There's some tradeoff between network overhead and latency — we can tune flush intervals. We'll share recommended parameters for Chrome and iOS.

[05:02] Priya: For benchmarking, we want a script that simulates our traffic (mix of short/long, streaming/non-streaming) and measures p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec. Can you provide one?
[05:12] Samir: Yes — Elena will attach a benchmarking harness (k6-based + token counters) and an example CSV for traffic profile. We'll also provide expected output template.

[05:20] Diego: One more on networking: do you support private link / direct VPC peering for Hosted to reduce egress and latency?
[05:28] Elena: We have VPC peering for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we offer PrivateLink for enterprise customers in supported regions — I'll note that and follow up with our network options doc.

[05:40] Liam: Security: SOC2, SSO (SAML/Okta), RBAC, data retention policies. Are logs redacted?
[05:48] Elena: We support SAML/OIDC SSO, granular RBAC, and can configure retention policies. By default logs can be retained for X days; for enterprise we offer longer retention and log export. Sensitive data can be redacted and we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).

[06:03] Priya: Cost question: do you meter tokens for streaming differently? Like per-token billed on final output only?
[06:09] Samir: We bill per-token produced plus some request overhead. Streaming doesn't change billing model — it's about tokens produced. For Dedicated there's a base reserved cost plus metered usage for bursts. We'll include sample cost models.

[06:25] Elena: Quick note: for token/sec numbers we used earlier, these are ballpark on our optimized runtime — actual results depend on prompt shape, conditioning length, and KV cache hit rates. That's why the pilot is important.

[06:40] Liam: Sounds reasonable. Pilot timeline? We could start small — run a week of generated traffic on hosted and compare to our internal self-hosted baseline.
[06:49] Samir: Agreed. Proposed pilot: 1 week of representative traffic on Hosted, Redwood runs token/sec and p95 captures, then a follow-up technical deep-dive to discuss Dedicated sizing and SLOs.

[06:59] Priya: For the pilot we need clear measurement: first-byte p95, full-response p95, tokens/sec, token jitter, and cost per 1k tokens. Can you deliver that?
[07:06] Elena: Yes. We'll produce a report with metrics and recommended dedicated pool size for your 250 qps baseline and 2x promotional spikes.

[07:15] Diego: On integration complexity: what SDKs? We use Node and a Go microservice.
[07:19] Samir: We have Rest SDKs, node, python, and go examples. Also WebSocket streaming examples for browsers.

[07:26] Priya: Any limits on max sequence length or special handling for KV cache?
[07:31] Elena: We support variable sequence lengths; KV cache size depends on model but our runtime manages cache eviction and sharing across sessions for dedicated pools. There are knobs for TTLs.

[07:43] Liam: Competitors — we've benchmarked Triton self-host and considered Vertex AI endpoints. Price/perf for open models is a big factor.

[07:51] Samir: Understood. We'll make sure the pilot includes a direct comparison matrix against your Triton numbers you share.

[07:59] Priya: Ok, let's recap next steps.
[08:02] Samir: Recap: (1) Elena shares security/compliance pack and benchmarking harness. (2) Samir sends dedicated pricing + SOW template. (3) Mera provides prompt set and traffic CSV. (4) Redwood runs 1-week hosted pilot and delivers report. (5) Schedule technical deep-dive after pilot.

[08:22] Liam: That covers it. Thanks everyone.
[08:25] Samir: Thanks — we'll follow up with an email and calendar invite.
[08:30] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings: "K V cache" appears as separate tokens in log; "SAML" sometimes transcribed as "Sam l". Some filler words removed for brevity.
notes: Customer target: p95 first-byte <= 300ms for short prompts; p95 <= 1.5s for longer responses
Peak baseline 250 qps, bursts 500 qps for 20–30 minutes
Pilot requested: 1-week hosted run with provided prompt set
Security pack and benchmarking harness to be shared promptly
